expected.rationale: as in the standard-layout condition, with one difference that is the reason this condition exists: the package is stored once in a content-addressed directory and linked into place, so an observed path may be either the link's or the real directory's. A mapping rule has to reach the same package from either

fixture_notes.vulnerable_package_selection: lodash 4.17.15, the same version as the standard-layout condition so the two differ only in layout. Verified against this image with the scanner used here: the same four HIGH findings, attributed to app/node_modules/.pnpm/lodash@4.17.15/node_modules/lodash/package.json
fixture_notes.layout: produced by the package manager itself rather than assembled by hand, so the link structure is the real one. The application-side path app/node_modules/lodash is a link to .pnpm/lodash@4.17.15/node_modules/lodash, and the scan report names the second
fixture_notes.system_call_level_truth: none; the system-call capture rate is reported as unavailable
fixture_notes.timestamp_precision: the timestamps are a wall-clock reading to the millisecond with a sub-millisecond part taken from a different clock. The two are not the same clock, so the digits below a millisecond are not a measurement of anything: treat the resolution as one millisecond, and keep the pairing tolerance well above it
